notes.meaning: Faith means being fully confident in what we hope for and certain of things we cannot see with our eyes. It is not a blind guess, but a deep trust grounded in God's faithfulness to his word. Faith acts like an inner sight, making God's unseen promises real and solid to our hearts.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some Word of Faith teachers explain faith as a tangible force or substance that God used to create the world and that believers can release, rather than simply trusting God's promises.

notes.meaning: God gave his approval to the ancient fathers and mothers because of their faith. Scripture praises their lives not for worldly success, but for their steady trust in God through hard times. Their stories stand as a witness to encourage everyone who follows after them.

Through faith, we understand that God created the entire universe simply by speaking his command. The visible world was not put together from materials that already existed, but was made out of nothing. Trusting God as the maker of all things helps us believe that he can bring his promises into reality.

Abel brought an animal sacrifice that pleased God because he offered it with a trusting heart. By faith, Abel was commended as righteous, which means being accepted as right in God's eyes. Even though Abel died long ago, his faithful example still speaks powerfully to us today.

Enoch walked closely with God and pleased him, so God took him straight to heaven without dying. The Scriptures testified that his whole life brought joy to God before he was taken. God rewarded Enoch's persistent trust by freeing him from the power of physical death.

It is impossible to please God without faith. Anyone who wants to draw near to God in worship must believe that he really exists and that he rewards those who earnestly seek him. God delights when we trust his goodness and count on his promises.

God warned Noah about a great flood, something no one had ever seen happen before. In holy reverence, Noah believed God's warning and spent years building a giant wooden boat to save his household. His obedience proved the unbelieving world was wrong and showed that real righteousness comes through trusting God.

When God told Abraham to leave his native country for a new homeland, he obeyed immediately. He packed up his life and went out, even though he did not know where he was going. Faith gave Abraham the courage to step forward into the unknown guided only by God's promise.

Abraham lived in the promised land like a guest in a foreign country. He lived in movable tents alongside his son Isaac and grandson Jacob, who were given the very same promise. They did not try to seize the land by force, but waited patiently for God to fulfill his covenant.

Abraham was content to live in fragile tents because he was looking forward to a city with permanent foundations. That eternal city is heaven, designed and built entirely by God. Abraham kept his heart fixed on that everlasting home instead of building an earthly empire.

Even though Sarah was far past the normal age for having children, God gave her the strength to conceive. Although she had laughed at first, she came to trust that God was completely reliable to keep his promise. Faith relies on God's power when human strength has completely run out.

Abraham was so old that he was physically as good as dead regarding having children. Yet from this one frail man came a great multitude of descendants, as countless as the stars in the night sky and the grains of sand by the ocean. God showed that he can bring life and fulfill his word out of total impossibility.

All these patriarchs died while holding firmly to their faith, even though they did not receive the final promised blessings during their lifetime. They saw those future joys from far away and welcomed them with glad hearts. By admitting that they were only travelers and visitors on earth, they confessed that their true home lay ahead.

People who speak of themselves as travelers show that they are actively looking for a homeland of their own. They make it clear that they do not belong to the earthly places where they dwell. Their whole way of living points to their search for a true, permanent home.

If the patriarchs had spent their time longing for the country they had left behind, they had plenty of chances to pack up and go back. Nothing kept them from returning except their deliberate choice to trust God's promises. They refused to return to their old home because they were moving forward with God.

Instead of going back, they were longing for a much better country in heaven. Because they placed their whole confidence in him, God is not ashamed to be called their God. He has prepared a magnificent heavenly city for them where they will live in his presence forever.

When God put Abraham to the test, he was ready to offer his beloved son Isaac on the altar. In his heart and purpose, Abraham actually surrendered the child through whom all the blessings were supposed to come. He proved that he loved and trusted the Giver more than the gift.

This command was an intense trial because God had specifically promised that Abraham's offspring would come through Isaac. Sacrificing Isaac looked like it would destroy God's own covenant. Yet Abraham trusted that God's word could never fail, even when circumstances seemed contradictory.

Abraham reasoned that God had the power to raise Isaac from the dead to keep his promise. In a symbolic way, Abraham did receive Isaac back from death when God stepped in and stopped the sacrifice. This rescue pointed ahead to the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the tomb.

Guided by faith, Isaac spoke prophetic blessings over his sons Jacob and Esau concerning what would happen to them in the future. He trusted God to guide their paths, placing the younger Jacob first in line for the primary covenant blessing. Isaac believed that what God had promised would surely come to pass.

When Jacob was near death, he leaned on the top of his walking staff and worshipped God. In that frail moment, he gave a prophetic blessing to each of Joseph's sons, favoring the younger brother Ephraim as God directed. His worship at life's close showed that his lifelong confidence in God remained steady to the end.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: An older Latin translation read this as Jacob worshipping the top of Joseph's staff, which some early Catholic commentators understood as showing reverence to the staff as a symbol of authority.

notes.meaning: As Joseph lay dying in Egypt, he spoke with absolute certainty about the future exodus, when God would bring Israel back to their homeland. He gave strict instructions that his bones must be carried along with them when they left. His unburied coffin stood as a constant witness that Egypt was not their final resting place.

Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born because they recognized that he was an extraordinary child favored by God. They refused to let fear of the Egyptian king's cruel order make them destroy their baby boy. Faith gave them the boldness to obey God rather than wicked human rulers.

When Moses grew into adulthood, he made a clear and courageous choice. He refused to hold onto the royal rank and privileges of being called the son of Pharaoh's daughter. Faith led him to turn his back on royal power so that he could belong entirely to God's people.

Moses chose to suffer alongside God's beaten-down people instead of enjoying the short-lived pleasures of sin in Pharaoh's court. He knew that the delights of the palace would soon vanish, while God's promises would last forever. Real faith chooses to do what is right even when it brings temporary pain.

Moses considered the shame of suffering for the promised Messiah to be worth far more than all the gold in Egypt. He kept his eyes focused on the eternal reward that God reserves for his faithful servants. Believers can endure hardship when they realize that following Christ brings riches that never fade.

By faith, Moses led the people out of Egypt without trembling before the king's furious anger. He stood firm and kept going because his spiritual eyes were fixed on the invisible God. When we stay focused on God's great presence, worldly threats lose their power over us.

Moses obeyed God by setting up the Passover and instructing Israel to smear the blood of a lamb on their doorposts. He trusted God's warning that the angel of death would strike Egypt's firstborn while passing over every blood-marked home. That protective blood looked forward to the salvation provided by Jesus' blood on the cross.

The people of Israel walked through the middle of the Red Sea on dry ground because they trusted God's miraculous rescue. When the Egyptian army tried to chase after them without faith, the divided waters crashed back down and drowned them all. God makes a way of safety for those who trust his guidance.

The massive defensive walls of Jericho came crashing down after the Israelite army marched around them for seven days in obedience to God. Humanly speaking, blowing horns and marching could never break stone walls, but God shattered them in answer to their trust. Faith wins victories when we follow God's commands even if they seem unusual.

Rahab the prostitute was spared from destruction because she welcomed the Israelite spies in peace. She believed what she had heard about the true God and chose to side with him rather than her rebellious neighbors. God's grace warmly receives anyone who turns to him in faith, no matter what their past has been.

The writer mentions that time runs out before he can share the full stories of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and all the prophets. Each of these leaders relied on God through difficult struggles in Israel's history. Even though they had human flaws, God did remarkable things through their faith.

Through faith, these heroes conquered hostile kingdoms, ruled their people with justice, and saw God's special promises fulfilled. Others relied on God in terrible danger, such as Daniel when God closed the mouths of hungry lions. Faith gives ordinary believers the strength to stand firm and do what is right.

Trusting in God quenched the burning fury of fiery furnaces and helped people escape the sharp edge of the sword. God transformed their natural weakness into strength, making them brave warriors who drove back foreign armies. God often uses our weakest moments to show his mighty power.

Grieving mothers, such as the widows helped by Elijah and Elisha, received their dead children back to life. At the very same time, other faithful believers were tortured and refused an easy escape on sinful terms so they might receive a far greater resurrection to eternal life. Faith is just as victorious when enduring hardship as it is when escaping pain.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic scholars point to the account of believers refusing release under torture as a clear reference to Second Maccabees chapter 7, which supports the authority of the deuterocanonical books.

notes.meaning: Other servants of God had to face cruel teasing, painful whippings, heavy chains, and dark prison cells. They endured these harsh trials simply because they refused to compromise their loyalty to God. Faith does not guarantee physical comfort, but it gives the grace to remain faithful through abuse.

Faithful prophets were stoned to death, sawed in two, and killed by the sword. Many had to dress in rough sheepskins and goatskins, living in extreme poverty, hunger, and oppression. Their willingness to lose everything showed that they prized God above life itself.

The cruel world thought these believers were unfit to live, but in reality the world was not worthy of having them. They were driven out to wander through desolate wildernesses and hide inside cold caves and holes in the ground. God honors his persecuted people even when society rejects and mistreats them.

All these people received God's high praise because of their genuine faith. Yet none of them lived to see the central promise fulfilled on earth, which was the arrival of the Messiah and his completed salvation. They kept trusting God's word even though the greatest blessing still lay in the future.

God had arranged something far better for us by sending Jesus Christ to finish his saving work. Those old covenant saints could not reach full spiritual completion apart from us, because all believers are brought to perfection together through Christ. Through Jesus, both Old and New Testament believers share one united and complete salvation.
